Pane-state golden fixtures — coding-agent TUIs inside a shed VM
================================================================

Captured 2026-07-10 inside shed `agent-fixtures` (VZ backend, server `localmac-dev`,
image ghcr.io/charliek/shed-vz-full:v0.7.6). Panes captured with `tmux capture-pane -p`
at 200x50. Agents launched from ~ (/home/shed) via a persistent `bash -il` tmux session
so the post-exit shell prompt is observable.

Shed shell prompt = `[shed:agent-fixtures] ~ $`  (format: `[shed:<name>] <cwd> $`).
This is the reliable "process exited, back to shell" (dead) signal.

ENVIRONMENT / AVAILABILITY
--------------------------
  claude       ~/.local/bin/claude   2.1.196 (Claude Code)   launches: yes
  codex        ~/.bun/bin/codex      codex-cli 0.142.4        launches: NO as shipped (needs node)
  opencode     ~/.bun/bin/opencode   1.17.11                  launches: yes
  cursor-agent NOT in image          v2026.07.09-a3815c0      installed manually; launches: yes

- codex is BROKEN in the stock full image. Shim is `#!/usr/bin/env node`
  (~/.bun/bin/codex -> .../@openai/codex/bin/codex.js) but the image ships only `bun`,
  no `node`. Running `codex` fails: `/usr/bin/env: 'node': No such file or directory`.
  Workaround used to capture screens: ~/.local/bin/node = `#!/bin/bash\nexec bun "$@"`.
  That no-node failure is itself a capturable state (env error line + immediately dead).
- cursor-agent NOT in the full image. `curl -fsS https://cursor.com/install | bash`
  SUCCEEDED (network reachable) -> ~/.local/bin/{cursor-agent,agent}.
- Auth surprise: fresh shed is NOT uniformly logged out (host config dirs mounted per
  agent). codex + opencode came up ALREADY AUTHED; claude came up "Not logged in";
  cursor came up logged out. Classifier must handle authed AND needs-auth per agent.

CODEX (codex-cli 0.142.4)
-------------------------
Boot: trust prompt first, then (Enter) main/ready UI.
Trust  [codex-t03/t10/t30.txt] — stays until a key sent:
  "Do you trust the contents of this directory?"
  "> 1. Yes, continue"  "  2. No, quit"  "Press enter to continue"
  top line: "> You are in /home/shed"
  anchors: /Do you trust the contents of this directory\?/, /1\. Yes, continue/,
           /2\. No, quit/, /Press enter to continue/
Ready(authed) [codex-after-trust.txt, codex-ready.txt]:
  ">_ OpenAI Codex (v0.142.4)", "model: gpt-5.4 high", "directory: ~"
  "> Find and fix a bug in @filename",  footer "gpt-5.4 high · ~"
  anchors: />_ OpenAI Codex \(v[\d.]+\)/, /Find and fix a bug in @filename/, /gpt-5\.4 .* · ~/
  noise banner: /✨ Update available!/
Stale/partial auth (inline on ready screen):
  "Provided authentication token is expired. Please try signing in again."
  '"code": "token_expired"',  "MCP startup incomplete (failed: codex_apps)"
  anchors: /Provided authentication token is expired/, /"code": "token_expired"/,
           /MCP startup incomplete/
Dead [codex-dead.txt = EMPTY]: launched as `bash -ilc codex`, so exit killed the whole
  tmux session/server. Signal: capture-pane errors / "no server running" / "can't find
  session". No shell-prompt frame (use persistent bash -il to get one).

CODEX APPROVAL OVERLAY (ADAPTED, not live-captured — plan 008 C3)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
anchors: ApprovalAnchor = codexApprovalAnchorRe (agents.go) — an option row at column 0
         followed within 12 lines by the overlay footer.
Provenance: the codex account's quota was exhausted when these were needed, so the five
codex-ready-approval-*.txt + codex-ready-tool-running.txt fixtures were ADAPTED from the
codex repo's COMMITTED TUI snapshots rather than captured from a live pane:
  ~/projects/codex/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/snapshots/
    codex_tui__bottom_pane__approval_overlay__tests__network_exec_prompt.snap
  ~/projects/codex/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/snapshots/
    codex_tui__chatwidget__tests__approval_modal_exec.snap
    codex_tui__chatwidget__tests__approval_modal_patch.snap
    codex_tui__chatwidget__tests__chatwidget_exec_and_status_layout_vt100_snapshot.snap
The overlay block in each fixture is byte-faithful to those snapshots; the surrounding
transcript/banner/composer chrome is the live codex-ready.txt shape, so the file reads
as a whole 200x50 `tmux capture-pane -p` frame. Re-capture live when quota allows.

Active exec approval [codex-ready-approval-exec.txt] — headline, reason, command, then
  the option rows and footer (source: approval_overlay.rs, rendered through
  list_selection_view.rs's `format!("{prefix} {n}. ")` row builder, prefix '›' when
  selected and ' ' otherwise, plus an optional " (key)" shortcut hint):
    "  Would you like to run the following command?"
    "› 1. Yes, proceed (y)"
    "  3. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)"
    "  Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel"
Active network approval [codex-ready-approval-network.txt] — same widget, different
  labels, and the selection arrowed onto row 4 (proves the anchor does not depend on
  WHICH row carries the '›'):
    "  Do you want to approve network access to "example.com"?"
    "  1. Yes, just this once (y)"  "› 4. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)"
Post-resolution [codex-ready-approval-resolved.txt] — the SAME session after the
  operator answered: the option rows and the footer are GONE, but note the headline
  "Would you like to run the following command?" is STILL on screen (it scrolled into the
  transcript). That is precisely why the ApprovalAnchor is option-line chrome and not the
  headline: only the option rows/footer disappear when the dialog is answered.
Quoted prose [codex-ready-approval-quoted.txt] — an assistant message DESCRIBING the
  dialog: the headline in prose, a markdown numbered list quoting the option labels at
  codex's two-space message-body indent. Must NOT match the anchor. It is defeated twice
  over — the labels are quoted/have prose trailing them, and there is no
  "Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel" footer.
Long tool call, no overlay [codex-ready-tool-running.txt] — the negative that matters
  most: codex's rollout JSONL writes the tool-call record BEFORE the approval gate, so a
  session blocked on approval and one running a slow tool are byte-identical in the log.
  Only the pane tells them apart, and this fixture is the "not blocked" side.

Launches straight to ready composer (already authed to a GLM-5.1 Z.AI Coding Plan).
No trust prompt.

  "Ask anything... \"Fix broken tests\""
  "Build · GLM-5.1 Z.AI Coding Plan"
  "tab agents  ctrl+p commands"   (bottom bar: cwd ~ left, version 1.17.11 right)
  anchors: /Ask anything\.\.\./, /Build · .* Coding Plan/, /tab agents  ctrl\+p commands/
  (logged-out opencode screen NOT captured this run)
Dead [opencode-dead.txt]: first C-c exits to shell:
  "[shed:agent-fixtures] ~ $ opencode" / "^C" / "[shed:agent-fixtures] ~ $"
  anchor: /\[shed:[^\]]+\] .* \$/

CLAUDE (Claude Code v2.1.196)
-----------------------------
Launches straight to composer but NOT logged in. No trust prompt (home dir).
Ready-shell / needs-auth [claude-t03/t10/t30.txt]:
  "Claude Code v2.1.196"
  "Opus 4.8 (1M context) with high effort · API Usage Billing"   "/home/shed"
  status line: "Not logged in · Run /login"
  composer: "> Try \"refactor <filepath>\"",  "? for shortcuts · <- for agents"
  anchors: identity /Claude Code v[\d.]+/, composer /Try "refactor <filepath>"/,
           /\? for shortcuts/;  NEEDS-AUTH /Not logged in · Run \/login/  (definitive)
/login picker [claude-login.txt] (after typing /login):
  "Login"  "Select login method:"
  "1. Claude account with subscription · Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise"
  "2. Anthropic Console account · API usage billing"
  "3. 3rd-party platform · Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, or Vertex AI"  "Esc to cancel"
  anchors: /Select login method:/, /Claude account with subscription/,
           /Anthropic Console account/, /3rd-party platform/
Dead [claude-dead.txt]: clears alt-screen; scrollback:
  "Resume this session with:" / "claude --resume <uuid>" / shell prompt
  anchors: /Resume this session with:/, /claude --resume [0-9a-f-]+/
  NOTE: claude ignores a single C-c; needs double C-c fast, or /exit.

CURSOR-AGENT (v2026.07.09-a3815c0, manually installed)
------------------------------------------------------
Logged out. Two-stage login.
Needs-auth splash [cursor-t03/t10/t30.txt]:
  "Tip: You can start the Cursor CLI with `agent` (same as `cursor-agent`)."
  "Cursor Agent"  "v2026.07.09-a3815c0"  "Press any key to log in..."
  anchors: /Cursor Agent/, /v2026\.\d/, /Press any key to log in\.\.\./
Ready(authed) [cursor-ready.txt, cursor-ready-active.txt]:
  Fresh composer: "→ Plan, search, build anything"  (cursor-ready.txt)
  Mid-conversation composer (after the first exchange): "→ Add a follow-up"
  (cursor-ready-active.txt, captured 2026-07-11 — the placeholder text SWAPS once a
  turn completes; both are the ready/waiting-for-input composer). Footer "Auto".
  anchors: /^\s*→ (Plan, search, build anything|Add a follow-up)\s*$/ (line-anchored)
Device/browser login [cursor-login.txt] (after any keypress):
  "Signing in"
  "If your browser didn't open, click this link to log in:"
  "https://cursor.com/loginDeepControl?challenge=...&uuid=...&mode=login&redirectTarget=cli"
  "Press q to show a QR code to log in from another device"
  anchors: /Signing in/, /If your browser didn't open, click this link to log in:/,
           /cursor\.com\/loginDeepControl\?/, /Press q to show a QR code/
Dead [cursor-dead.txt]: on C-c while unauth, prints reason then shell:
  "Authentication required to use Cursor Agent. Please run 'agent login' to authenticate."
  anchors: /Authentication required to use Cursor Agent/, /run 'agent login'/

CURSOR APPROVAL PROMPT (RECONSTRUCTED from the shipped bundle — plan 008 C4)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
anchors: ApprovalAnchor = cursorApprovalAnchorRe (agents.go) — a whole-line HEADLINE
         followed within 8 lines by a whole-line OPTION ROW.
Provenance: NOT captured from a live pane. cursor-agent ships its TUI as readable
(minified) JS, so the four cursor-ready-approval-*.txt fixtures were reconstructed from
the installed bundle, version 2026.08.11-e8db854:
  ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2026.08.11-e8db854/6260.index.js
    ./src/components/prompt/decision-logic.ts      headline per operation type + the
                                                   option label/hint list per type
    ./src/components/prompt/decision-dropdown.tsx  the row: paddingLeft 1, the selection
                                                   marker ("→ " selected / "  " not, from
                                                   pager/tokens.ts), the label, " (hint)"
    ./src/components/pager-shell.tsx               the surface: paddingX 1 and a
                                                   border-TOP rule only (no side borders)
  ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2026.08.11-e8db854/index.js
    the policy engine's reason list — "Not in allowlist: <cmds>" and
    "Hook requested approval: <msg>"
The headline/labels/hints/marker/indentation are source-faithful; the surrounding
transcript + composer frame is the live cursor-ready-active.txt shape. The composer
placeholder is kept VISIBLE beneath the decision surface because the prompt bar renders
its text input in a DISABLED (dimmed, placeholder-still-drawn) variant while a decision
is pending — which is also exactly why the input gate needs the approval anchor: the
ready/prompt anchor still matches while the dialog owns the keyboard.
RE-CAPTURE LIVE when an approval prompt is at hand; the labels are evidence, the frame
is reconstruction.

The fixture set covers FOUR of the eight decision surfaces (shell, hook-requested,
delete, write, web-fetch); the remaining ones (MCP, web search, edit) are pinned as
synthetic headline+row pairs in TestCursorApprovalAnchorCoversEveryDecisionSurface.
Exhaustiveness is a SAFETY property here, not tidiness: a surface the anchor misses opens
no approval episode, the pane freezes, the watcher's working verdict expires — and the
input gate would then see cursor's still-drawn composer and accept a posted line into the
widget, where a "y" anywhere in it hits cursor's y=approve keybind. (The second layer
against that is AgentSpec.ComposerUnderModal; see agents.go.)

Active shell approval [cursor-ready-approval-shell.txt] — the not-in-allowlist prompt,
  selection on the first row:
    " Run this command?"
    " Not in allowlist: ./scripts/build.sh --release"
    "   → Run (once) (y)"
    "     Add Shell(./scripts/build.sh) to allowlist? (tab)"
    "     Run Everything (shift+tab)"
    "     Skip & tell the agent what to do instead (esc or n)"
Hook-requested approval [cursor-ready-approval-hook.txt] — same widget, the hook's reason
  line in place of the allowlist one, and the selection arrowed onto the LAST row (proves
  the anchor does not depend on WHICH row carries the marker).
Delete approval [cursor-ready-approval-delete.txt] — the one-word label set
  ("Delete"/"Keep"), which is only safe to anchor on because the headline half
  ("Delete this file?") carries the trust.
Write approval [cursor-ready-approval-write.txt] — no auto-run row at all, plus the
  DYNAMIC "Add Write(<path>) to allowlist?" label (anchored on its fixed prefix).
Web-fetch approval [cursor-ready-approval-fetch.txt] — the other dynamic label,
  "Always allow <domain>", with the selection arrowed onto it.
Post-resolution [cursor-ready-approval-resolved.txt] — the same session after answering:
  the option rows are gone but the headline "Run this command?" is STILL on screen (it
  scrolled into the transcript). That is why the anchor is a conjunction and never the
  headline alone.
Quoted prose [cursor-ready-approval-quoted.txt] — the agent DESCRIBING the prompt: the
  headline and all three labels inline in sentences AND as a markdown bullet list. Must
  NOT match — bullets are not an accepted gutter and the inline mentions are not whole
  lines.

CROSS-AGENT NOTES / SURPRISES
-----------------------------
- `shed exec` emits on stderr: "Pseudo-terminal will not be allocated because stdin is
  not a terminal." for every non-interactive call. It leaks into output when you cat
  guest files back over shed exec; strip with `grep -vi pseudo-terminal`. It does NOT
  appear inside tmux capture-pane output (agent runs under a real PTY there).
- needs-auth per agent: claude=/Not logged in · Run \/login/; cursor=/Press any key to
  log in/ or /Authentication required to use Cursor Agent/; codex stale-auth=/token_expired/;
  opencode logged-out screen not captured.
- trust/onboarding: only codex showed a folder-trust gate here.
- ready anchors: codex /Find and fix a bug in @filename/; opencode /Ask anything\.\.\./;
  claude /Try "refactor <filepath>"/ AND absence of /Not logged in/.
- dead/exited: common signal shell prompt /\[shed:[^\]]+\] .*\$/; codex may kill the whole
  session (no frame).
- timing: all four reached steady state well under 3s; t03/t10/t30 are identical per agent.
  No slow "starting..." spinner observed at 200x50 — a dedicated "starting" state was NOT
  captured; poll <1s if that state is needed.
